minutes.headline: Reconstituted Board of Assessors met for the first time, nominated a chair, and tentatively set its next meeting for October 11.
minutes.summary: The newly reconstituted board introduced itself and heard public comment from a select board member and a resident urging impact reviews, a communication plan and an abatement-surge protocol. A chair nomination was made and seconded, and meeting day and time were discussed without being settled. The interim principal assessor briefed the board on new construction, the Vision revaluation kickoff, delayed estimated bills, and items to sign.

Urged the board to list and prioritize issues, act as a unit, and communicate promptly.
Urged preserving assessment data outside the application and updating the assessors map when tax bills go out.
Supported yearly static database exports with trends available to the public.

Delays described as a cost of poor quality.

what_happened.line: The reconstituted Board of Assessors held its first meeting; a chair nomination was made and seconded, but the vote was not audible on the recording.
The board tentatively targeted Wednesday, October 11 for its next meeting, then Monday evenings at a location still to be confirmed.
The interim principal assessor briefed the board on new construction, the Vision revaluation kickoff, delayed estimated bills, and documents to sign.
A resident urged an impact review, a public communication plan and a protocol for a surge of abatement filings, noting staff are down hours.
The board agreed to add a standing policy review item to future agendas and set the next meeting for October 11 at 6:45, location to be found.

why_it_matters: The assessors set the property valuations behind each tax bill, and this board is deciding how it will handle a revaluation, new commercial construction and a possible wave of abatement requests.
Who chairs the board is not confirmed in the recording, so a resident cannot yet tell from it who is responsible for the schedule and for answering abatement questions.
watch_next: Next meeting tentatively October 11 at 6:45, location not yet found.
The official minutes, to confirm whether the chair vote passed.

reconciliation.what: Our minutes against the minutes the town published. caption_error = the same fact the captions rendered badly, resolved by the official reading shown beside the as-heard one; discrepancy = a substantive difference, flagged and not resolved. reconciliation.summary: The records agree on the chair nomination, the October 11 6:45 next meeting and the standing agenda policy review item, but official has many more votes and action items than ours. The main thing to know: the Vice Chair and Clerk votes, public comment and most assignments appear only in the official minutes, while our dollar figures (13 million, 1.3 million) have no counterpart in the official text.
